title: OpenSSH on musl without PAM can accept passwords for accounts without password hashes
summary: OpenSSH before 10.6p2 on Linux with musl and PAM disabled can permit password authentication without knowing a password under specific account configurations. Alpine publishes backported package fixes and requires restarting sshd after updating.

severity.rationale: CISA now lists this authentication bypass as exploited in the wild. Exploited account access can reach developer credentials and code execution, warranting 24 hours; the musl, PAM and account prerequisites still determine exposure.

affected.product: Portable OpenSSH on Linux with musl and PAM disabled
affected.note: Distribution backports must be checked separately.

exposure: Alpine documents password authentication enabled, an account with a * password field and another account with a $5$ or $6$ hash. The ordinary openssh-server package lacks PAM; openssh-server-pam with UsePAM no is affected, while UsePAM yes is unaffected. Root is reachable when PermitRootLogin allows passwords or when an exposed account can escalate, for example through doas. Official Alpine tiny-cloud images 3.18.11 through 3.24.3 ship an alpine user with a * password and passwordless doas; they become exploitable when any $6$ hash exists. Containers without sshd are not exposed through this path.

params.instructions: Identify the running SSH server's package, libc, PAM and password-authentication settings. Compare upstream against 10.6p2 or the exact Alpine branch package floor in this advisory; do not flag vendor backports solely by upstream version.

remediation.details: Install OpenSSH 10.6p2 or the vendor backport and restart sshd. If updating is delayed, disable password authentication and restart sshd after validating configuration. Verify key login first and retain an existing session while testing a fresh login.
remediation.risk: Medium. Restarting or changing authentication can interrupt automation or lock out administrators.

remediation.details: Search authentication logs for Accepted password for entries involving accounts without passwords, including root and key-only users. Review doas activity, newly created users and files, and authorized keys. If an unauthorized login cannot be ruled out, treat the system as compromised.
remediation.risk: Medium. Investigation and compromise response can interrupt services; installing the fix does not establish that earlier access did not occur.

verification: Confirm the running daemon uses the fixed package after restart.
If using containment, verify effective PasswordAuthentication is no, including applicable Match conditions, and test a new key login.
Complete the Alpine compromise checks for exposed systems; unresolved evidence of a possible login requires treating the system as compromised.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.
